metadata.name: Pauline Hanson
metadata.description: Australian senator advocating tighter immigration, shared national culture, lower taxes and strategic public stakes in natural resources.
metadata.scope: Current documented governing or campaigning position through 4 October 2026. Recent conduct is prioritised; earlier material is used only as a stated continuity-based inference. Party proposals are attributed as the leader’s endorsed programme, not implemented law. Every answer is an interpretive assessment, with lower confidence for biomedical hypotheticals and fine-grained psychological causation. No scores were targeted.

review.notes: Independent audit read all 240 exact questions and all 15 briefs/counters. Reopened One Nation issue, resource, education, firearms, immigration and family-tax pages; parliamentary speech via OpenAustralia; ABC June parental-leave and July migration reports; added September migration and qualified-apology evidence. Corrected sporting/occupational firearm rights versus personal defence, family restriction, eight-year welfare wait versus permanent exclusion, minority equity versus general public ownership, ABC criticism versus privatisation, currency coexistence, progressive tax brackets, work conditions versus benefit expiry, family transfers above subsistence, cultural holidays versus official religion, religious fiscal privilege, voluntary medical availability versus mandates, overstrong hypothetical risk positions, national versus state municipal approval, and overconfident racial self-control inference. Recorded September remarks as counter-evidence without converting rhetoric into a genetic causal theory. Removed repeated whole-brief boilerplate. Portrait metadata retained; no score tuning. Neutral warnings reflect conditional positions under the owner-authorised inference rule. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
